newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices rise as strikes, cold bite into supplies.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices rise as strikes, cold bite into supplies.

text.p: World oil prices surged higher on Thursday as cold weather and refinery strikes in France ate into supplies of refined products amid robust consumer demand, traders said.
International marker crude Brent Blend for January delivery on the International Petroleum Exchange in London closed at $24.64 a barrel, up 85 cents from Wednesday's finish.

Oil prices have been consolidating at higher levels despite the prospect of imminent Iraqi oil sales because of strong demand in a fairly balanced market vulnerable to any potential supply disruption.
"Underlying fundamentals are very powerful," said Peter Gignoux, who heads the energy desk at Smith Barney in London.
A London broker said cold weather across Europe and falling stocks of natural gas in the United States were among other factors pulling prices higher in keeping demand for heating oil strong.
Prompt gas oil, which is used as a heating fuel in Europe, closed $5.50 a tonne higher on the IPE with January futures not far behind.

Heating oil stocks on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean have been at historically low levels and the strike at Elf's three refineries in France has forced the company to look elsewhere for refined products to meet commitments in an already tight market.
The strike is expected to spread to a Shell refinery on December 9 and could extend to an industry-wide one-day strike on December 10, French union officials said.
France's largest union said on Thursday it would recommend that striking Elf workers keep up their action after company concessions on pay failed to address strikers' concerns over job cuts.

Strong Chinese demand has pushed Singapore gas oil prices to a level which attracts European sellers, who are able to take advantage of higher prices for refined products in the Far East and the United States.
"There are a lot of arbitrage opportunities; first gasoline to the United States and now gas oil to Asia," a broker said.
